entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the 3rd respondent, Insurance Company in O.P (MV) No.120 of 2008 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Pala.
The respondents herein were the petitioners before the tribunal.

2. The facts leading to the case before the tribunal is as follows:- On 15.03.2007, while the deceased was returning from his work place at Pala in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-35-2721, a lorry bearing Reg.No.-7M-6318 applied sudden break due to which the motorcycle hit the lorry and thereby he sustained serious injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
The legal heirs approached the tribunal claiming compensation under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
3. Before the tribunal respondents 1, 2 and 3 were the driver, owner and insurer of the offending vehicle respectively.
Respondents 1 and 2 remained ex parte.
The 3rd respondent, insurer, filed a written statement contending that the petition is not maintainable either in law and on facts.
Before the tribunal, the evidence consists of documentary evidence as Exts.A1 to A4 and B1 were marked.
The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and material on record awarded a total compensation of 4,84,700/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum.
Challenging the liability to pay the compensation amount awarded by the tribunal, the appellant insurer has come up with the above appeal.

4. Heard the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant insurer and the learned counsel for the respondents/claimants.
5.

The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that at the time of filing this appeal, the appellant had raised contention that there was negligence on the part of the deceased rider of the motorcycle and hence contended that the insurer is not liable to pay the amount.

However, it is fairly submitted that the position is now covered by the judgment of the Apex Court in United India Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Sunil Kumar and another [2017 KHC 5644]
wherein it is categorically stated that under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, the Court, for awarding compensation need not look into the aspect of negligence.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Sunil Kumar and another [2017 KHC 5644]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even negligent persons are entitled for compensation under Section 163A of the act.
Hence, I do not find any merit in this appeal.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
